The denominator is $1+3\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $1-3\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $1-3\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6+\text{i}}{1+3\text{i}} & =\frac{6+\text{i}}{1+3\text{i}}\cdot \frac{1-3\text{i}}{1-3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{(6+\text{i})(1-3\text{i})}{(1+3\text{i})(1-3\text{i})} \\  & =\frac{6-18\text{i}+\text{i}-3{\text{i}}^{2}}{{1}^{2}-(3\text{i})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{6-17\text{i}-3(-1)}{1-(-9)} \\  & =\frac{9-17\text{i}}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\frac{9-17\text{i}}{10}=(\frac{9}{10})+(-\frac{17}{10})\,\text{i}.
$$
